title: Closing an account: only at zero or with its money moved out or written off, owed accounts paid to zero first, links moved first, and its schedules end on the closing day
written_in: SCHEMA_V3 3, 5; DECISIONS_ROUND2 O (close, never delete), P6, Q7, Q (write-off), R3, R4, R5, S3
notes: Every amount is made up and in whole minor units (yen).

Question `close` [P6]: closing `account` on `date` with its final figure `figure` (the final `check`). `transfers` are the transfers out that the closing asks for, `{ to, a }`. The account closes only when the figure less the transfers is zero; otherwise the closing is refused and `left` shows what is still in it. On a close the answer gives `closed` (the date), the events written (the final `check`, then each transfer, all dated the closing day) and `ends`: each schedule of the account (paid from it, landing in it, or a transfer into it) with its new `ends`, the closing day, unless it already ends on or before that day. Other schedules are untouched.

[Q7] The closing's transfer out, or its write-off, has the built id `close:<account>`, so the same closing written on two devices is one record (merge.json mg-70). [S3] A closing that writes several records (a transfer and a write-off, or transfers to two accounts) names them `close:<account>:1`, `:2`, in the order written: the transfers as listed, then the write-off (merge.json mg-71 to mg-73).

[Q watch item] Closing may write off a balance that cannot be moved out (a few pesos in a dead e-wallet): `writeOff` is that amount, written as a spend from the account dated the closing day, id `close:<account>`; with it the figure less the transfers less the write-off must be zero.

[R3] `kind` is the account's type (left out: bank). A card, loan or pay-later account whose `figure` (what it still owes) is above zero, or a bank whose figure is below zero, cannot be closed: the answer is refused with `owes` (an owed account) or `left` (a bank below zero) and `offer`, the payment that gets it to zero: a `repay` from the account's `payFrom` into it, or for a bank a `transfer` into it from an account the person picks (no `acct`).

[R4] `links` lists what hangs on the account: `cards` paid from it and `places` kept in it. Each needs a new account in `newLinks` (`{ <card or place id>: <account id> }`) before the closing goes on; without one the closing is refused with `needs`, the links still to move. A close answer with links gives `links`, each moved to its new account.
[R5] 38.31 has no closed accounts (one bank figure), so the move brings in nothing closed; there is no case for it.

cases.question: close
cases.title: An account at zero closes; its bill ends on the closing day
cases.why: The final figure is 0, so nothing has to move out and the account closes [P6]. The gym is paid from it, so its schedule ends on Fri 8 Jan; the pay lands in the main bank and is untouched.

cases.question: close
cases.title: 30,000 left, moved out by the transfer the closing asks for: it closes
cases.why: 30,000 (final figure) - 30,000 (moved to the main bank) = 0, so it closes [P6]. The final check holds the figure; the transfer moves it out on the same day, with the built id `close:old` [Q7]. As scenarios/account_closed.json.

cases.question: close
cases.title: Money left and no transfer: the closing is refused
cases.why: 30,000 is still in it and nothing moves it out, so it is not closed [P6]; the 30,000 is shown and nothing is written.

cases.question: close
cases.title: A transfer that moves out only part: refused, with what is still in it
cases.why: 30,000 - 20,000 = 10,000 still in it, which is not zero, so it is not closed [P6].

cases.question: close
cases.title: A transfer of more than the final figure: refused
cases.why: 30,000 - 35,000 = -5,000: the transfer would take 5,000 the account does not hold, so it is not zero and the closing is refused [P6].

cases.question: close
cases.title: Every schedule of the account ends on the closing day; one that already ended keeps its end
cases.why: The gym (paid from it, ending 31 Dec), a side income landing in it and a top-up transfer into it from the main bank are its schedules: each ends on Fri 8 Jan [P6]. The phone already ended on 5 Jan, before the closing day, and keeps that end. The rent is paid from the main bank and is untouched.

cases.question: close
cases.title: A dead e-wallet with 3.50 left that cannot be sent: written off as a spend, id close:<account>
cases.why: Pesos, in centavos. 3.50 (final figure) - 3.50 (written off) = 0.00, so it closes [P6 and the Q watch item]. The write-off is a spend from the e-wallet dated the closing day, with the built id `close:g` [Q7] (scenarios/closing_write_off.json).

cases.question: close
cases.title: A card that still owes 20,000: refused, and the payment that gets it to zero is offered
cases.why: A card that still owes money cannot be closed until it is at zero [R3]; the closing screen offers the payment that gets it there: 20,000 from its paying account, the main bank.

cases.question: close
cases.title: A loan with 150,000 still owed: refused, its payment offered
cases.why: A loan that still owes money cannot be closed until it is at zero [R3]: 150,000 from the account that pays it is offered.

cases.question: close
cases.title: A bank 5,000 below zero: refused, a transfer in of 5,000 offered
cases.why: A bank below zero cannot be closed until it is at zero [R3]: 5,000 moved into it gets it there, from an account the person picks.

cases.question: close
cases.title: A card paid off to zero closes; its schedules end
cases.why: The card owes nothing, so it closes [R3, P6]; a subscription paid on it ends on the closing day [P6].

cases.question: close
cases.title: The bank a card is paid from and a goal is kept in: refused until each has a new account
cases.why: Closing the account a card is paid from, or a goal is kept in, first asks for the new account and moves the link; it cannot close until one is picked [R4]. Neither is picked yet.

cases.question: close
cases.title: New accounts picked for the card and the goal: the links move, the money moves out, it closes
cases.why: The card is now paid from the new bank and the trip is kept in it [R4]. 30,000 (final figure, the trip's money included) - 30,000 (moved to the new bank, `close:old`) = 0, so it closes [P6, Q7].

cases.question: close
cases.title: A new account picked for the card only: still refused for the goal
cases.why: The card has its new paying account; the trip has none yet, so the closing cannot go on [R4].

cases.question: close
cases.title: Most of a dead e-wallet moved to the bank, the rest written off: two records, close:g:1 and close:g:2
cases.why: Pesos, in centavos. 1,003.50 (final figure) - 1,000.00 (moved to the bank) - 3.50 (written off) = 0.00, so it closes [P6, Q watch item]. The closing writes two records, named in the order written: the transfer `close:g:1`, then the write-off `close:g:2` [S3]. Before S3 neither had a built id (accounts-open-4).

cases.question: close
cases.title: An old bank's money moved to two accounts: close:old:1 and close:old:2, in the order listed
cases.why: 50,000 (final figure) - 30,000 (to the main bank) - 20,000 (to the second bank) = 0, so it closes [P6]. Two records: `close:old:1` and `close:old:2`, in the order the closing writes them [S3].

cases.question: close
cases.title: Closing the main bank asks for the new main bank first
cases.why: The old bank is `home.mainBank`. Closing it asks for the new main bank before anything else; until one is picked the closing is refused [T watch decided, R4].

cases.question: close
cases.title: Closing the main bank moves every link to the new main bank: the main bank, the lines and Free to spend on it, the pay schedules
cases.why: 200,000 (final figure) - 200,000 (to the new bank) = 0, so it closes [P6]. The new main bank is the new bank: `home.mainBank`, Food and Free to spend (on the main bank, no account of their own) and the pay schedule move to it [T watch decided]; the car line is on another account and stays. The phone bill paid from the old bank ends on the closing day [P6].
